title: Humaans is coming to US payroll
summary: US payroll is coming to Humaans, rolling out with first customers this fall. CEO Giovanni Luperti on why payroll, why the US, and what AI changes about both.
body_markdown:
When we started Humaans, our ambition was to build the best foundation for people operations in the world: clean data, flexible workflows, and infrastructure that is built for how scaling companies actually operate. As we've grown with increasingly complex and global organizations, we've seen how much more becomes possible when you get that foundation right, both in the software we can build on top of it and in what organizations can do with their people data across the systems they rely on.


Payroll is a natural extension and a clear example of what becomes possible on that foundation. It is one of the most critical processes a company runs, and almost everything required to run it correctly starts with the workforce data Humaans already holds and the changes happening across it.


Today, we're taking a major step forward and announcing Humaans Payroll for the US. We'll begin rolling it out with our first customers this fall.


## **Compounding the Humaans platform**


Over the last few years, we've been steadily compounding an incredible amount of high-quality software on top of the Humaans system of record, expanding what organizations can do from a single, deeply connected foundation.


Most recently, we launched our new AI Employee Engagement capabilities, helping companies understand how their organization feels, uncover patterns across teams over time, and use AI to turn large volumes of feedback into meaningful insights and action. Earlier this year, we introduced Athena, our system-agnostic, agentic AI platform, built to automate work by deploying AI agents capable of operating across People, IT and Finance


Now we're bringing US payroll into that foundation.


## **Why payroll. Why the US.**


The US is a market we care deeply about and one where we're investing significantly.


A growing portion of our business already comes from US companies, while the majority of the international organizations we work with either already have employees in the US or are actively expanding there. We want Humaans to support these companies as they grow, while keeping their workforce data and operations deeply connected as they scale.


We also believe US payroll represents an enormous product opportunity. It's a large and complex market, still served by many legacy solutions that companies don't particularly love but are forced to adopt. Multi-state workforces, taxes, benefits, different employment arrangements and constant changes across the organization create enormous operational complexity.


We believe there's a significant opportunity to bring the Humaans approach to this category: exceptional product quality, powerful and flexible infrastructure, clean and deeply connected data, and AI at the core of the experience. More broadly, AI is forcing organizations to rethink how they operate and the technology they build around. We're seeing a massive appetite for a new generation of software that doesn't simply make existing processes easier, but fundamentally changes how work gets done and drives measurable business impact.


More fundamentally, payroll is a natural extension of the workforce record. Everything required to pay someone correctly is the consequence of events the system of record already owns: someone joins, moves state, gets promoted, changes compensation, takes leave or receives a bonus. Yet every pay cycle, teams still spend enormous amounts of time reconstructing that context for payroll.


We think payroll should work differently. It shouldn't begin when someone sits down at the end of a pay cycle to prepare it. It should begin the moment a decision is made to change something in the workforce. Payroll should be deeply connected to the workforce record, so changes flow naturally into the payroll process with the right context, effective dates and approvals, rather than requiring teams to reconstruct what happened at the end of every pay cycle.


## **Reimagining workplace technology for the AI era**


This becomes even more important as we think about the impact AI will have on how companies operate. We don't believe the next generation of workplace technology will look like today's SaaS products with an AI assistant added on top. AI changes what software itself can do: from giving people better tools to complete work, to understanding context, reasoning across systems, and increasingly executing that work on their behalf. That's the shift we're designing Humaans around.


Historically, HR software has been designed primarily to record what happened. It stores the employee, their employment, compensation, location, working patterns, policies, approvals and the history of how those things changed. Individuals are then responsible for almost everything that needs to happen as a consequence: noticing the change, moving data between systems, checking policies, coordinating approvals, reconciling results and resolving exceptions.


Payroll creates another critical execution layer for the AI-native platform we're building. Athena can reason across the workforce record, policies, workflows and connected systems, while payroll gives it the ability to understand and act on the financial consequences of workforce changes. A promotion can result in the appropriate compensation change being approved, its payroll impact understood and prepared automatically, exceptions identified, and anything requiring judgment surfaced to the right person. The people remain in control, while increasingly less of their time needs to be spent moving information around and administering the process.


That's ultimately the direction we're building toward: moving beyond software that just records how an organization operates, toward software that understands what's happening and increasingly helps operate the organization.


## **What we're building towards**


We're moving deeper into the US, further upmarket, and into more of the critical infrastructure our customers rely on to run their organizations. We're continuing to compound the breadth and depth of the Humaans platform while fundamentally rethinking what that platform can become in an AI-native world.


Payroll is a major step in that journey. We'll begin rolling out Humaans Payroll with our first US customers this fall, and I'm incredibly excited about what comes next. 🇺🇸
